key_insight: In long axisymmetric channels, diffusio-osmotic flow from concentration gradients is essentially unchanged by adding a pressure drop, but channel geometry can either amplify or suppress the flow and strongly tune ionic flux.
engineering_relevance: This gives micro- and nanofluidic designers a geometry-based way to predict, control, and separate fluid and ionic transport using channel shape and an effective cylinder approximation.
method: Derive transport theory for electrolyte flow in long axisymmetric channels with thin diffuse layers.
Decompose total flow into diffusio-osmotic and pressure-driven components and compute Δp(Q) relations.
Map how channel geometry affects hydrodynamic resistivity and ionic flux, including a simple equivalent-cylinder model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical calculations for several axisymmetric channel shapes, with nearly linear Δp(Q) curves and shape-dependent slopes, supporting the approximation and design claims.
watch_item: The theory assumes diffuse layers are thin relative to the local channel radius, so accuracy may degrade in strongly overlapping double-layer or very small-channel regimes.
paper_title: Diffusioosmosis of electrolyte solutions in axisymmetric channels
